title: Why You Break Eye Contact With Strangers
hook: You instinctively look away when someone stares at you.

narration.text: You instinctively look away when someone stares at you.
This is a common social boundary response, not shyness.
Prolonged eye contact can feel threatening, even if unintended.
Your brain interprets it as a challenge or an invasion of space.
Breaking eye contact restores a sense of psychological comfort.
It helps manage social interactions smoothly and respectfully.
Next time you feel this, notice the urge; like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more insights into human behaviour.

description: Ever wonder why you instinctively look away when someone holds your gaze for too long? It is not always shyness. This video explores the fascinating psychological reasons behind breaking eye contact.
topic: Why you tend to look away when someone makes prolonged eye contact. This is a common social boundary response.
